pages.text:
MCP (Model Context Protocol) | TranscriptAPI.com Skip to content MCP (Model Context Protocol) Use TranscriptAPI to fetch transcripts, search YouTube, browse channels, and list playlists â all from within your AI assistant via Model Context Protocol (MCP). Claude Tutorial Complete guide to integrate TranscriptAPI with Claude AI assistant via
MCP. Recommended ChatGPT Tutorial Step-by-step guide to connect TranscriptAPI with ChatGPT using OAuth
authentication. Agent Builder Tutorial Learn how to set up TranscriptAPI with OpenAI Agent Builder for AI
workflows. YouTube Transcript MCP Server Section titled âYouTube Transcript MCP Serverâ TranscriptAPI runs a hosted (remote) MCP server at https://transcriptapi.com/mcp . Add that URL to an MCP client and your AI assistant can fetch YouTube transcripts, search YouTube, and list a channelâs or playlistâs videos. There is nothing to install or host. The server uses the same account, API keys, and credits as the REST API . Server URL: https://transcriptapi.com/mcp Authentication: OAuth 2.1 (Claude, ChatGPT) or an API key sent as a Bearer token (OpenAI Agent Builder and other clients). See Authentication . Tools: 12, covering transcripts, video info and metadata, search, channels, and playlists. See Available Tools . Cost: 2 tools cost no credits. The others use 1 credit per call, or 1 credit per page of results. New accounts get 100 free credits. See Credit Cost . Supported Clients Section titled âSupported Clientsâ Client How it connects Auth Setup guide Claude (claude.ai, Claude Desktop) Custom connector (remote MCP) OAuth Claude guide ChatGPT Plugin on ChatGPT web (custom MCP server) OAuth (Client ID and Secret) ChatGPT guide OpenAI Agent Builder MCP server in an agent workflow API key Agent Builder guide Claude Code TranscriptAPIâs YouTube agent skills (no MCP config needed) API key, set up on first use Claude Code guide Cursor, Windsurf Remote MCP server ( url + headers config) or TranscriptAPIâs YouTube agent skills API key API key configuration OpenClaw TranscriptAPIâs YouTube skill API key, set up on first use OpenClaw guide Any other MCP client Remote MCP server URL OAuth 2.1 or API key Server configuration Writing your own code instead? The REST API exposes the same data. See the Python , JavaScript , and cURL quick starts. What is MCP? Section titled âWhat is MCP?â Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standardized framework that enables AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT to connect directly with external tools and data sources. With TranscriptAPIâs MCP integration, your AI can fetch YouTube transcripts on-demand without manual copy-pasting or switching between applications. Key Benefits: Direct integration into your AI workflow No manual transcript fetching needed Consistent, structured data format Works with any MCP-compatible platform Why Use TranscriptAPI with MCP? Section titled âWhy Use TranscriptAPI with MCP?â TranscriptAPI offers unique advantages for YouTube Transcript MCP integration: Universal Compatibility Section titled âUniversal Compatibilityâ TranscriptAPI works with any platform that supports MCP . Whether your platform uses OAuth for seamless authentication (like Claude and ChatGPT) or requires manual API key configuration (like OpenAI Agent Builder), we provide both options to ensure maximum compatibility. Proven Reliability Section titled âProven Reliabilityâ Battle-tested with major AI platforms Consistent performance across all authentication methods Same powerful transcript extraction engine as our REST API Flexible authentication options (OAuth or API Key) based on your platformâs requirements Prerequisites Section titled âPrerequisitesâ Before setting up TranscriptAPI with MCP, ensure you have: A TranscriptAPI account ( sign up free ) An AI assistant or platform that supports MCP For OAuth: A web browser for the initial authorization For API Key: An active API key from your dashboard MCP Server Configuration Section titled âMCP Server Configurationâ Get your MCP configuration details from the MCP dashboard or use these settings: Property Value Server Name Transcript API Server URL https://transcriptapi.com/mcp Description Use TranscriptAPI to fetch YouTube video transcript automatically Icon Download Icon Quick Setup Visit your MCP dashboard for a personalized setup guide with these configuration details and authentication options tailored to your chosen platform. Authentication Section titled âAuthenticationâ TranscriptAPI supports two authentication methods to work with different MCP platforms: OAuth (Recommended) API Key OAuth Authentication Section titled âOAuth Authenticationâ OAuth provides automatic, secure authentication without manual key management. Supported by: Claude (Dynamic Client Registration - optional credentials) ChatGPT (Static Client Registration - requires Client ID/Secret) Any MCP client supporting OAuth 2.1 Two Registration Methods: TranscriptAPI supports both Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) and Static Client Registration to work with different platforms: 1. Dynamic Client Registration (Claude, optional) Claude and other clients that support DCR can automatically register No Client ID/Secret needed - just add the MCP server URL The client automatically discovers OAuth endpoints and registers itself Youâll be redirected to authorize access (one-time) 2. Static Client Registration (ChatGPT, required) ChatGPT requires Client ID and Client Secret upfront Get your credentials from the MCP Integration dashboard Expand Advanced: Static OAuth Credentials , click Create New Client , name it, then click Generate Credentials Copy your Client ID and Client Secret In ChatGPT on the web, open Plugins , click the plus button, choose Add custom MCP server , enter the server URL, choose OAuth and paste them in Check I understand and want to continue , click Create as a plugin , install the plugin, then type @ in a new chat to select it How it works: Add the MCP server URL to your client For ChatGPT: Add Client ID and Client Secret For Claude: Credentials are optional (DCR supported) The client automatically discovers our OAuth endpoints Youâll be redirected to authorize access (one-time) Tokens are managed automatically with refresh support Technical Details: Uses OAuth 2.1 with both Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) and Static Registration Authorization server metadata: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server Protected resource metadata: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource Required scope: mcp:access Access tokens prefixed with oat_ Benefits: No manual key management (for DCR clients) Automatic token refresh Secure, time-limited access Revocable permissions Platform-specific support (ChatGPT and Claude) API Key Authentication Section titled âAPI Key Authenticationâ API Key authentication provides simple, direct access for platforms that donât support OAuth. Required for: OpenAI Agent Builder Custom MCP implementations Development/testing environments How it works: Get your API key from the API Keys dashboard Add it to your MCP client configuration The key is sent as a Bearer token with each request Configuration: the standard url + headers format for remote MCP servers, used by clients such as Cursor and Windsurf: { "mcpServers" : { "transcriptapi" : { "url" : " https://transcriptapi.com/mcp " , "headers" : { "Authorization" : " Bearer sk_your_api_key_here " } } } } Technical Details: Bearer token authentication: Authorization: Bearer sk_... API keys prefixed with sk_ Keys never expire (unless manually revoked) Same key works for both REST API and MCP Security Best Practices: Store keys in environment variables Never commit keys to version control Use separate keys for different environments Rotate keys regularly Available Tools Section titled âAvailable Toolsâ TranscriptAPI exposes 12 tools through MCP: Tool Description Cost get_youtube_transcript Fetch video transcript as markdown or JSON 1 credit get_youtube_video_info Basic metadata + available transcript languages (pick a language first) Free get_video_metadata Rich video metadata; optional details (duration, tags, captions) + related 1 credit search_youtube Search videos, channels, playlists, or movies â with sort/date/duration filters 1 credit/page get_channel_info Channel profile: title, handle, counts, tags, banners, available tabs 1 credit get_channel_latest_videos Get latest ~15 videos from a channel (RSS) Free search_channel_videos Search within a specific channel 1 credit/page list_channel_videos Paginated channel feed â videos (default), shorts , or streams 1 credit/page list_channel_playlists Paginated list of a channelâs playlists 1 credit/page list_channel_posts Paginated community (Posts tab) content 1 credit/page get_channel_sections Curated channel sections ( featured Home, podcasts , releases ) 1 credit list_playlist_videos Paginated list of playlist videos 1 credit/page All channel tools accept flexible input: @handle , full YouTube URL, or UC... channel ID. Which video tool? Use get_youtube_video_info (free) to discover transcript languages before fetching a transcript. Use get_video_metadata (1 credit) for view/like counts, publish date, description, duration, tags, or related videos. get_youtube_transcript Section titled âget_youtube_transcriptâ Extract transcripts from any YouTube video with full control over the output format. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description video_url string required YouTube video URL or 11-character video ID send_metadata boolean true Include video title, author, and thumbnail format string "text" Output format: "text" (markdown) or "json" (structured) include_timestamp boolean true Include timestamps with each segment language string none Comma-separated priority list, e.g. de,en,asr . Omit for English, or the videoâs first available language. asr = auto-generated captions Accepted URL Formats: Full URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ Short URL: https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ Video ID only: dQw4w9WgXcQ Example Usage: // Get transcript as markdown with metadata (default) get_youtube_transcript ({ video_url: " https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ " }) // Returns: { " content " : " # Metadata 
 ## Title: Rick Astley - Never Gonna Give You Up 
 ## Author: RickAstleyVEVO 
 ## Author URL: https://www.youtube.com/@RickAstley 
 ## Thumbnail: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/dQw4w9WgXcQ/hqdefault.jpg 

 # Transcript 
 [0.0s] Never gonna give you up 
 [4.12s] Never gonna let you down... " } // Get JSON format without metadata get_youtube_transcript ({ video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " , format: " json " , send_metadata: false }) // Returns: { " content " : { " transcript " : [ { " text " : " Never gonna give you up " , " start " : 0.0 , " duration " : 4.12 }, { " text " : " Never gonna let you down " , " start " : 4.12 , " duration " : 3.85 } ] } } // Get plain text without timestamps get_youtube_transcript ({ video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " , format: " text " , include_timestamp: false , send_metadata: false }) // Returns: { " content " : " # Transcript 
 Never gonna give you up Never gonna let you down Never gonna run around and desert you... " } Output Formats: Text Format (Default) JSON Format Returns markdown-formatted text with optional metadata header and timestamped transcript lines. # Metadata ## Title: Video Title Here ## Author: Channel Name ## Author URL: https://www.youtube.com/@ChannelName ## Thumbnail: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/VIDEO_ID/hqdefault.jpg # Transcript [ 0.0s ] First line of transcript [ 3.5s ] Second line of transcript [ 7.2s ] Third line of transcript Returns structured data with transcript segments and optional metadata. { "transcript" : [ { "text" : " First line of transcript " , "start" : 0.0 , "duration" : 3.5 }, { "text" : " Second line of transcript " , "start" : 3.5 , "duration" : 3.7 } ], "metadata" : { "title" : " Video Title Here " , "author_name" : " Channel Name " , "author_url" : " https://www.youtube.com/@ChannelName " , "thumbnail_url" : " https://i.ytimg.com/vi/VIDEO_ID/hqdefault.jpg " } } get_youtube_video_info Section titled âget_youtube_video_infoâ Free (no credit used). Basic metadata (title, author, thumbnail) plus the list of available transcript languages â call this before get_youtube_transcript to pick a language. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description video_url string required YouTube video URL or 11-character video ID Each returned language code (e.g. en , or asr-en for auto-generated English) can be passed to get_youtube_transcript âs language parameter. For counts, publish date, description, duration, tags, or related videos, use get_video_metadata . get_youtube_video_info ({ video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " }) get_video_metadata Section titled âget_video_metadataâ Rich video metadata without needing captions: title, view/like-count text, publish date, structured description + links, uploading-channel summary, and thumbnails. Costs 1 credit. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description video_url string required YouTube video URL or 11-character video ID include string[] none Extras: "details" (duration, category, tags, caption tracks) and/or "related" (related videos) Hidden counts are null , never 0 . When details canât be read, details.available is false with a reason instead of guessed values. // Metadata only get_video_metadata ({ video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " }) // With player details + related videos get_video_metadata ({ video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " , include: [ " details " , " related " ] }) search_youtube Section titled âsearch_youtubeâ Search YouTube for videos, channels, playlists, or movies (paginated, ~20 results per page). Returns structured results with video IDs, titles, view counts, and thumbnails, plus a continuation_token for the next page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description query string none The search query (first call). search_type string "video" Type of search: "video" , "channel" , "playlist" , or "movie" (first call only). sort string "relevance" First-page sort: "relevance" or "views" . upload_date string none First-page upload window (videos only): hour , today , week , month , year . duration string none First-page duration bucket (videos only): short (under 4m), medium (4â20m), long (over 20m). continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls). Provide either query (first call) or continuation (next pages) â not both. Filters apply to the first call only ; the continuation token already encodes them. An empty page can come back while has_more is true â keep following the token until has_more is false . Costs 1 credit per page. Example Usage: // First call search_youtube ({ query: " TED talk artificial intelligence " , search_type: " video " }) // Returns: { " content " : { " results " : [ { " video_id " : " abc123 " , " title " : " The future of AI | TED Talk " , " channel " : " TED " , " view_count " : " 2.5M views " , " published " : " 2024-03-15 " , " thumbnail " : " https://i.ytimg.com/vi/abc123/hqdefault.jpg " } // ... more results ], " continuation_token " : " 4qmFsgKlARIY... " , " has_more " : true } } // Next page â use continuation token search_youtube ({ continuation: " 4qmFsgKlARIY... " }) get_channel_latest_videos Section titled âget_channel_latest_videosâ Get the ~15 most recent videos from a YouTube channel via RSS. Free â no credits consumed. When YouTubeâs feed is unavailable, published is approximate: the list then comes from the channelâs uploads, and publish times are worked out from times like â9 hours agoâ. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string required Channel identifier: @handle , channel URL, or UC... ID Accepted Input Formats: Handle: @TED URL: https://www.youtube.com/@TED Channel ID: UCsT0YIqwnpJCM-mx7-gSA4Q Example Usage: get_channel_latest_videos ({ channel: " @TED " }) // Returns: { " content " : { " channel " : { " name " : " TED " , " url " : " https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCsT0YIqwnpJCM-mx7-gSA4Q " }, " results " : [ { " video_id " : " xyz789 " , " title " : " The next breakthrough in AI " , " published " : " 2024-06-01 " , " thumbnail " : " https://i.ytimg.com/vi/xyz789/hqdefault.jpg " } // ... up to ~15 results ] } } search_channel_videos Section titled âsearch_channel_videosâ Search for videos within a specific YouTube channel (paginated, ~30 results per page). Costs 1 credit per page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string none Channel identifier: @handle , channel URL, or UC... ID (first call). query string none Search query within the channel (first call). continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls). Provide either ( channel + query ) (first call) or continuation (next pages) â not both. Example Usage: // First call search_channel_videos ({ channel: " @TED " , query: " education " }) // Returns: { " content " : { " results " : [ { " video_id " : " def456 " , " title " : " The future of education | TED Talk " , " view_count " : " 1.2M views " , " published " : " 2024-01-20 " , " thumbnail " : " https://i.ytimg.com/vi/def456/hqdefault.jpg " } // ... more results ], " continuation_token " : " 4qmFsgKlARIY... " , " has_more " : true } } // Next page â use continuation token search_channel_videos ({ continuation: " 4qmFsgKlARIY... " }) list_channel_videos Section titled âlist_channel_videosâ List a channelâs feed with pagination. Use tab to choose the uploads feed (default, ~100/page), Shorts, or live streams (~48/page). Costs 1 credit per page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string none Channel identifier: @handle , URL, or UC... ID (first call) tab string "videos" Which feed: videos (uploads), shorts , or streams (live). Repeat the same tab when paginating. continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls) Provide either channel (first call) or continuation (next pages) â not both. Example Usage: // First call â start listing list_channel_videos ({ channel: " @TED " }) // Returns: { " content " : { " results " : [ { " video_id " : " ghi789 " , " title " : " How AI could empower any business " , " view_count " : " 800K views " , " published " : " 2024-05-10 " } // ... ~100 results ], " continuation_token " : " Ehl... " , " has_more " : true } } // Next page â use continuation token list_channel_videos ({ continuation: " Ehl... " }) get_channel_info Section titled âget_channel_infoâ A channelâs profile: title, @handle , verified flag, subscriber/video-count text, description, keywords, tags, thumbnails, banners, and the tabs it exposes. Not paginated. Costs 1 credit. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string required Channel identifier: @handle , URL, or UC... ID Counts are display strings (e.g. 27.8M subscribers ) and null when YouTube hides them â never 0 . Check availableTabs before calling get_channel_sections or list_channel_videos with a tab . get_channel_info ({ channel: " @TED " }) list_channel_playlists Section titled âlist_channel_playlistsâ Paginated list of the playlists on a channel (id, title, URL, video-count text, thumbnails). Costs 1 credit per page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string none Channel identifier: @handle , URL, or UC... ID (first call) continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls) Provide either channel or continuation â not both. Pass a returned playlist id to list_playlist_videos to get its videos. list_channel_playlists ({ channel: " @TED " }) list_channel_posts Section titled âlist_channel_postsâ Paginated list of a channelâs community (Posts tab) content â text, publish time, like-count text, and attachments (image, multi-image, video, playlist, or poll). Costs 1 credit per page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string none Channel identifier: @handle , URL, or UC... ID (first call) continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls) Provide either channel or continuation â not both. Channels without a community tab return an empty results list (not an error). list_channel_posts ({ channel: " @TED " }) get_channel_sections Section titled âget_channel_sectionsâ The curated, grouped sections of a channel page â titled shelves of videos, playlists, shorts, or featured channels, in the channelâs own order. Not paginated. Costs 1 credit. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string required Channel identifier: @handle , URL, or UC... ID tab string "featured" Which curated page: featured (Home), podcasts , or releases podcasts and releases exist only on channels that have them (empty results otherwise â call get_channel_info to see a channelâs tabs). get_channel_sections ({ channel: " @TED " }) get_channel_sections ({ channel: " @TED " , tab: " releases " }) list_playlist_videos Section titled âlist_playlist_videosâ List videos in a YouTube playlist with pagination (~100 per page). Costs 1 credit per page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description playlist string none Playlist URL or ID starting with PL , UU , LL , FL , or OL (first call) continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls) Provide either playlist (first call) or continuation (next pages) â not both. Example Usage: // First call â start listing list_playlist_videos ({ playlist: " UUAuUUnT6oDeKwE6v1NGQxug " }) // Returns: { " content " : { " results " : [ { " video_id " : " jkl012 " , " title " : " Introduction to Machine Learning " , " channel " : " TED-Ed " , " published " : " 2024-02-15 " } // ... more results ], " continuation_token " : " Qmx... " , " has_more " : true } } // Next page â use continuation token list_playlist_videos ({ continuation: " Qmx... " }) Platform Integration Section titled âPlatform Integrationâ TranscriptAPI MCP works with any platform that supports the Model Context Protocol . Here are guides for popular platforms: Tested Platforms Section titled âTested Platformsâ Connect to Claude - OAuth authentication support Connect to ChatGPT - OAuth authentication support Connect to OpenAI Agent Builder - API key authentication Universal Compatibility Section titled âUniversal Compatibilityâ TranscriptAPI works with any tool, framework, or custom implementation that supports MCP: OAuth-enabled platforms : Automatic authentication and token management API key platforms : Manual configuration with your TranscriptAPI key Custom implementations : Choose the authentication method that fits your needs Future-Proof Integration As new MCP-compatible platforms emerge, TranscriptAPI will work with them out of the box. Our standards-compliant implementation ensures long-term compatibility. Credit Usage & Rate Limits Section titled âCredit Usage & Rate Limitsâ MCP requests consume credits and are subject to rate limits just like REST API calls: Credit Cost Section titled âCredit Costâ Tool Cost get_youtube_transcript 1 credit get_youtube_video_info Free get_video_metadata 1 credit search_youtube 1 credit per page get_channel_info 1 credit get_channel_latest_videos Free search_channel_videos 1 credit per page list_channel_videos 1 credit per page list_channel_playlists 1 credit per page list_channel_posts 1 credit per page get_channel_sections 1 credit list_playlist_videos 1 credit per page Only charged on successful (HTTP 200) responses Failed requests (4xx, 5xx) donât consume credits Rate Limits Section titled âRate Limitsâ 200 requests per minute on Starter Monthly, 300 requests per minute on Starter Annual and OpenClaw (more on request) Limits apply per account , shared by all your API keys and OAuth tokens See API Rate Limits for detailed information and best practices. Monitor Your Usage MCP tools may make multiple requests during a conversation. Monitor your credit usage in the dashboard to avoid unexpected consumption. Error Handling Section titled âError Handlingâ All MCP tools return user-friendly error messages that AI assistants can understand and communicate: Common Errors Section titled âCommon Errorsâ Error Code Description Retry? Solution 401 Invalid authentication â Check your API key or re-authorize OAuth 402 Insufficient credits â Purchase more credits or upgrade plan 404 Transcript not available â Video may not have captions or be private 408 Timeout / Retry â Temporary failure - retry after 1-5 seconds 422 Invalid YouTube URL â Provide a valid YouTube URL or video ID 429 Rate limit exceeded â Wait before retrying (see Retry-After header) 500 Server error â ï¸ Temporary issue, contact support if persistent 503 Service unavailable â Service temporarily down - retry after 1-5 seconds Error Response Format Section titled âError Response Formatâ Errors are returned in a format that AI assistants can easily interpret: { "content" : " Unable to fetch transcript: Payment required. You have no credits remaining. Please purchase more credits at https://transcriptapi.com/dashboard/billing " } The AI assistant will communicate these errors naturally to the user. Best Practices Section titled âBest Practicesâ Security Section titled âSecurityâ OAuth platforms : Let the platform handle token storage and refresh API key platforms : Store keys in environment variables, never in code Rotate API keys regularly for enhanced security Monitor usage through the dashboard to detect anomalies Performance Section titled âPerformanceâ Batch requests when possible to stay within rate limits Cache transcripts locally if you need them multiple times Handle 402 errors gracefullyâinform users about credit status Implement exponential backoff for retries on 408/429/503 errors Integration Tips Section titled âIntegration Tipsâ Test with common videos first to ensure configuration works Provide context to the AI about video content for better responses Use metadata to give AI information about video source and author Choose the right format : JSON for structured processing, text for natural language Development Workflow You can develop and test with API keys for quick setup, then switch to OAuth for production deployments when supported by your platform. Troubleshooting Section titled âTroubleshootingâ OAuth Issues Section titled âOAuth Issuesâ âAuthorization failedâ : Clear browser cookies and try again âInvalid redirectâ : Ensure youâre using the latest MCP client version Token expiration : OAuth tokens auto-refresh; if issues persist, re-authorize API Key Issues Section titled âAPI Key Issuesâ âInvalid API keyâ : Verify key starts with sk_ and is active in dashboard âNo creditsâ : Check credit balance at /dashboard/billing Key not working : Ensure no extra spaces when copying the key General Issues Section titled âGeneral Issuesâ No transcript returned : Video might not have captions available Slow responses : Check if video is very long (>2 hours) Connection errors : Verify your internet connection and firewall settings Next Steps Section titled âNext Stepsâ Ready to get started? Hereâs what to do next: Get your credentials : Sign up and get an API key or prepare for OAuth Choose your platform : Select from our platform-specific guides Configure MCP : Follow the configuration examples above Test it out : Try fetching a transcript from a YouTube video Explore the API : Check our REST API Reference for advanced usage Need live testing? Try our Swagger UI to experiment with the API directly. Frequently Asked Questions Section titled âFrequently Asked Questionsâ What is a YouTube transcript MCP server? It is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that gives an AI assistant a tool for fetching YouTube transcripts. TranscriptAPIâs server is hosted at https://transcriptapi.com/mcp , so the assistant calls it directly and you donât run anything on your own machine. Besides transcripts, it can search YouTube and list channel and playlist videos. Which AI assistants work with the TranscriptAPI MCP server? Claude and ChatGPT connect with OAuth, and OpenAI Agent Builder connects with an API key. Each has a step-by-step guide: Claude , ChatGPT , OpenAI Agent Builder . Other clients that support remote MCP servers can connect with OAuth 2.1 or an API key sent as a Bearer token. See Supported Clients . Do I need to install or host anything? No. TranscriptAPI hosts the MCP server. You add the server URL in your AI client, then either sign in through OAuth or add your API key. How much does the YouTube MCP server cost? New accounts get 100 free credits with no card required. The get_youtube_video_info and get_channel_latest_videos tools cost no credits. The other tools use 1 credit per call, or 1 credit per page for paginated results. Failed requests donât use credits. Calls still need a verified email and an account with credits or a plan. Paid plans start at $5 per month for 1,000 credits. See Credit Cost . Is the MCP server the same as the REST API? It uses the same account, API keys, and credits as the TranscriptAPI REST API and the same transcript extraction. You can try a workflow in an AI assistant and later call the REST API from your own code. Can the MCP server get transcripts in other languages? Yes. The get_youtube_video_info tool, which costs no credits, lists the transcript languages a video offers, and get_youtube_transcript accepts a language priority list such as de,en . Codes starting with asr are YouTubeâs auto-generated captions. Related Section titled âRelatedâ API Reference Complete REST API documentation with examples and parameters. Getting Started Quick start guide for TranscriptAPI basics and setup. Contact Support Get help with technical issues or account questions.

pages.text: YouTube Transcript API in JavaScript (Node.js) | TranscriptAPI.com Skip to content YouTube Transcript API in JavaScript (Node.js) This page shows how to get a YouTube transcript in JavaScript with TranscriptAPI. You send one HTTPS request with a video URL or ID and get back the transcript as JSON segments or plain text. The examples use Node.js and the built-in fetch , so there is nothing to install. Prefer another language? See the Python and cURL quick starts. Before you start Section titled âBefore you startâ An API key. Sign up to get 100 free credits (no card required), then copy a key from the API Keys dashboard . Node.js 18 or newer , which includes fetch . Check with node --version . Your key in an environment variable , so it never ends up in your code: Terminal window export TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY = " your_api_key " The examples use top-level await , so save them as .mjs files. Each successful transcript request costs 1 credit. Failed requests (4xx and 5xx) cost nothing. See Credit Usage & Billing . Keep the key on the server Call TranscriptAPI from Node.js, a serverless function, or another backend. Donât put your API key in browser JavaScript, where anyone can read it. If a browser app needs transcripts, have it call your own backend route instead. Get a transcript Section titled âGet a transcriptâ Save this as transcript.mjs and run node transcript.mjs : const API_KEY = process . env . TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY ; const params = new URLSearchParams ( { video_url: " https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ " , } ); const response = await fetch ( ` https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/transcript? ${ params } ` , { headers: { Authorization: ` Bearer ${ API_KEY } ` } }, ); if ( ! response . ok ) { throw new Error ( ` ${ response . status } : ${ JSON . stringify ( await response . json ()) } ` ); } const data = await response . json (); console . log ( data . video_id , data . language , data . lengthText ); for ( const segment of data . transcript . slice ( 0 , 3 )) { console . log ( ` [ ${ segment . start } s] ${ segment . text } ` ); } video_url accepts a full URL ( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=... ), a short URL ( https://youtu.be/... ), or the 11-character video ID. Response (shortened): { "video_id" : " dQw4w9WgXcQ " , "language" : " en " , "transcript" : [ { "text" : " [âªâªâª] " , "start" : 1.36 , "duration" : 1.68 }, { "text" : " âª We're no strangers to love âª " , "start" : 18.64 , "duration" : 3.24 }, { "text" : " âª You know the rules \n and so do I âª " , "start" : 22.64 , "duration" : 4.32 } ], "length_seconds" : 213 , "lengthText" : " 3:33 " } Each segment has the caption text , its start time in seconds, and its duration in seconds. The full field list is in the API Reference . Check a video first (free) Section titled âCheck a video first (free)â Not every video has a transcript. Before you spend a credit, ask GET /youtube/info . It takes the same video_url as the transcript endpoint. The API Reference says âno credit is consumedâ and âThe same API key and active plan are required as for the transcript endpoint.â A 200 gives you the videoâs metadata ( title , author_name , author_url , thumbnail_url ) and available_languages , a list of code , name , and kind entries. A 404 means the video does not exist or has no captions, so there is nothing to fetch. const API_KEY = process . env . TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY ; const BASE_URL = " https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2 " ; const headers = { Authorization: ` Bearer ${ API_KEY } ` } ; const params = new URLSearchParams ( { video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " } ); // No credits: does the video exist, and does it have captions? const info = await fetch ( ` ${ BASE_URL } /youtube/info? ${ params } ` , { headers } ); if ( info . status === 404 ) { console . log ( " No transcript for this video: " , ( await info . json ()) . detail ); } else if ( ! info . ok ) { throw new Error ( ` ${ info . status } : ${ JSON . stringify ( await info . json ()) } ` ); } else { const { metadata , available_languages } = await info . json (); console . log ( metadata . title , " by " , metadata . author_name ); console . log ( " Languages: " , available_languages . map ( ( lang ) => lang . code )); // 1 credit: now fetch the transcript const response = await fetch ( ` ${ BASE_URL } /youtube/transcript? ${ params } ` , { headers } ); if ( ! response . ok ) throw new Error ( ` HTTP ${ response . status } ` ); const data = await response . json (); console . log ( data . transcript . length , " segments " ); } This check is most useful in batch jobs, where some videos in a list have no captions. Get plain text and save it to a file Section titled âGet plain text and save it to a fileâ Set format to text and include_timestamp to false to get the whole transcript as one string. Thatâs useful for LLM prompts, search indexes, or notes. Add send_metadata to get the video title and channel as well. import { writeFile } from " node:fs/promises " ; const API_KEY = process . env . TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY ; const params = new URLSearchParams ( { video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " , format: " text " , include_timestamp: " false " , send_metadata: " true " , } ); const response = await fetch ( ` https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/transcript? ${ params } ` , { headers: { Authorization: ` Bearer ${ API_KEY } ` } }, ); if ( ! response . ok ) throw new Error ( ` HTTP ${ response . status } ` ); const data = await response . json (); await writeFile ( ` ${ data . video_id } .txt ` , data . transcript , " utf8 " ); console . log ( " Saved transcript of: " , data . metadata . title ); With include_timestamp left at true , text output keeps one line per segment in the form [18.64s] text . Choose a transcript language Section titled âChoose a transcript languageâ /youtube/info costs no credits and lists the languages a video offers. Pass a comma-separated priority list in language and the API returns the first one that exists. The language field in the response tells you which one you got. Codes starting with asr are YouTubeâs auto-generated captions. const API_KEY = process . env . TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY ; const BASE_URL = " https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2 " ; const headers = { Authorization: ` Bearer ${ API_KEY } ` } ; // No credits: list the transcript languages a video offers const info = await fetch ( ` ${ BASE_URL } /youtube/info? ${ new URLSearchParams ( { video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " } ) } ` , { headers }, ) . then ( ( r ) => r . json ()); console . log ( info . available_languages . map ( ( lang ) => lang . code )); // 1 credit: German if available, otherwise English const data = await fetch ( ` ${ BASE_URL } /youtube/transcript? ${ new URLSearchParams ( { video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " , language: " de,en " } ) } ` , { headers }, ) . then ( ( r ) => r . json ()); console . log ( " Got: " , data . language ); If none of the requested languages exist, the API returns a 404 that lists the languages the video does have. See language for the full rules. Errors you might see Section titled âErrors you might seeâ Failed requests cost no credits. Every error response has a detail field. These are the ones you are most likely to meet. 401 Unauthorized. The API key is missing or wrong. The response has a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header and a short message: { "detail" : " Invalid API key " } Check that TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY is set in the environment that runs Node.js, and that the key still exists in the API Keys dashboard . Donât retry until you fix the key. 402 Payment Required. You have run out of credits, or you have no active plan. Here detail is an object with a reason and a link to fix it: { "detail" : { "message" : " You have an active plan, but you've run out of credits. " , "reason" : " insufficient_credits " , "action_label" : " Top up credits " , "action_url" : " https://transcriptapi.com/top-up " } } When reason is no_active_paid_plan , action_url points to Billing instead. Free endpoints such as /youtube/info also need an active plan, so they can return 402 too. Open action_url , then send the request again. 404 Not Found. There is no transcript to return. The code field tells you why: { "detail" : " No transcript available for video tfLTHCpPsSY " , "code" : " no_captions " } Other codes are video_unavailable , age_restricted , live_not_started , and no_transcript_for_requested_languages . The last one comes with an available_languages list you can retry with. Branch on code , not on detail . Donât retry the same request, except live_not_started after the stream has aired. Each code is explained in 404 error codes . 429 Too Many Requests. You went over your planâs rate limit, which all API keys on your account share. Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then retry. Rate-limited requests cost no credits. You might also see 422 when video_url is not a valid URL or video ID (fix the input), or 408 and 503 for a temporary failure (retry after a few seconds). Handle errors and retries Section titled âHandle errors and retriesâ Retry 408 , 429 , and 503 , and wait for the Retry-After header when the API sends one. Donât retry the other errors, because the request itself needs fixing. const API_KEY = process . env . TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY ; const RETRYABLE = new Set ([ 408 , 429 , 503 ]); const sleep = ( ms ) => new Promise ( ( resolve ) => setTimeout ( resolve , ms )); async function getTranscript ( videoUrl , options = {}, maxRetries = 3 ) { const params = new URLSearchParams ( { video_url: videoUrl , ... options } ); for ( let attempt = 0 ; attempt < maxRetries ; attempt ++ ) { const response = await fetch ( ` https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/transcript? ${ params } ` , { headers: { Authorization: ` Bearer ${ API_KEY } ` } } , ); if ( response . ok ) return response . json (); if ( RETRYABLE . has ( response . status ) && attempt < maxRetries - 1 ) { // Use Retry-After when the API sends it, otherwise back off 1s, 2s, 4s... const retryAfter = Number ( response . headers . get ( " Retry-After " )) || 2 ** attempt ; await sleep ( retryAfter * 1000 ); continue ; } // 401 bad key, 402 no credits, 404 no transcript, 422 invalid URL: don't retry const body = await response . json (); throw new Error ( ` ${ response . status } : ${ JSON . stringify ( body . detail ) } ` ); } } console . log (( await getTranscript ( " dQw4w9WgXcQ " )) . lengthText ); The full error list and response bodies are in Error Handling . Get transcripts for a channelâs latest videos Section titled âGet transcripts for a channelâs latest videosâ /youtube/channel/latest costs no credits and returns a channelâs 15 most recent uploads. It accepts an @handle , a channel URL, or a UC... ID. Each transcript you then fetch costs 1 credit. const API_KEY = process . env . TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY ; const BASE_URL = " https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2 " ; const headers = { Authorization: ` Bearer ${ API_KEY } ` } ; // No credits: the channel's 15 most recent uploads (RSS) const latest = await fetch ( ` ${ BASE_URL } /youtube/channel/latest? ${ new URLSearchParams ( { channel: " @TED " } ) } ` , { headers }, ) . then ( ( r ) => r . json ()); // 1 credit per transcript for ( const video of latest . results . slice ( 0 , 3 )) { const params = new URLSearchParams ( { video_url: video . videoId , format: " text " , include_timestamp: " false " , } ); const response = await fetch ( ` ${ BASE_URL } /youtube/transcript? ${ params } ` , { headers } ); if ( response . ok ) { const { transcript } = await response . json (); console . log ( video . title , " -> " , transcript . split ( / \s + / ) . length , " words " ); } else { console . log ( video . title , " -> no transcript " , response . status ); } } The same key also works for search , paginated channel videos , and playlists .
